beats.say: Hello! This lesson is about online dating. The scammer writes patiently for weeks, then asks for money.
It all starts with warm words: a lovely photo, a moving life story and messages every day.

body.text: Good morning! Writing to you is the best moment of my day.

beats.say: Then a problem suddenly appears: customs, a hospital or a great investment. And money is needed.
The rule: never send money or crypto to someone you have not met in person.

scenes.title: A new friend
scenes.intro: An engineer called Kamran writes to you on social media. Follow the chat as the weeks pass and decide.

body.text: Hi! I came across your photos and really liked them. I am an engineer on an offshore oil platform and rarely get to Baku.

steps.say: The first message. So far everything looks normal.

actions.label: Check his photo with a reverse image search
actions.feedback: Smart move. Fake profiles often use someone else's photos.

actions.label: Reply: nice to meet you
actions.feedback: Chatting is fine, but be careful. You have no friends in common and the profile is new.

actions.label: Send my phone number and workplace
actions.feedback: Do not rush to give personal details to a stranger. They can be used to pressure you later.

body.text: You are my first thought every morning.
Shall we do a video call?
I would love to, but the camera does not work on the platform and the internet is weak. I can only write.

steps.say: Two weeks have passed. Messages arrive every day.

actions.label: Insist on a video call
actions.feedback: Right. Avoiding video calls for weeks is a key sign of a fake profile.

actions.label: I understand, let's keep writing
actions.feedback: If there is always an excuse, the person may not be who they say they are.

body.text: Let me tell you a secret: I make 30 percent a month on KriptoNova. Start with 500 AZN, I will open your account:

steps.say: A month has passed. Suddenly the talk turns to money.

actions.label: No, I do not do money deals
actions.feedback: Right. Moving from romance to investment is a classic scam path.

actions.label: Open the link, just to look
actions.feedback: A fake platform shows profit charts but never lets you withdraw.

actions.label: Invest 500 AZN
actions.feedback: That money went to the scammer. A platform that promises guaranteed returns is fake.

body.text: I need help urgently. Customs is holding my equipment and wants a 1,800 AZN fee. My card is blocked abroad.
I will pay you back next week. Please do not tell anyone.

steps.say: Two more weeks have passed. Now there is a crisis.

actions.label: Send 1,800 AZN
actions.feedback: The money is gone and will not come back. Never send money to someone you have not met.

actions.label: Talk to my family first
actions.feedback: Well done. A request for secrecy is a warning in itself, and your family sees the situation from outside.

actions.label: Block and report profile
actions.feedback: Right. When a crisis and a money request come together, it is a scam.

body.text: So you do not trust me? I have no one but you...

steps.say: No money arrives, so the pressure grows.

actions.label: Block and report profile
actions.feedback: The right decision. Making you feel guilty is the scammer's last tool.

actions.label: I feel bad, I'll send the money
actions.feedback: The pressure worked and the money is gone. Someone who truly loves you would not blame you over money.

body.text: Thank you so much, my dear! Now customs wants insurance too, I need another 900 AZN.

steps.say: He got the money, and a new demand came at once.

actions.label: Stop, go to the bank and the police
actions.feedback: Right. A scammer never stops and finds a new reason after every payment.

actions.label: Send it one more time
actions.feedback: Every new payment makes the loss bigger. Stop and talk to your family.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs in Kamran's messages.

body.text: I work on an offshore oil platform and rarely get to Baku.
The camera does not work, I can only write.
I make 30 percent a month on KriptoNova.
Customs wants 1,800 AZN. Do not tell anyone.

spots.label: Working far away
spots.explain: Being offshore, abroad or on military duty is a ready excuse never to meet.

spots.label: No video calls
spots.explain: Avoiding video calls for weeks suggests the profile may be fake.

spots.label: Guaranteed profit
spots.explain: Moving from romance to investment is a classic scam path. Guaranteed returns do not exist.

spots.label: Secrecy and money
spots.explain: When a money request comes with secrecy, stop and talk to your family.

question.prompt: How can you check that Kamran is who he says he is?

options.label: Reverse image search his photo and ask for a video call
options.feedback: Right. These two checks are the simplest and most reliable.

options.label: Ask him for more photos
options.feedback: A scammer has plenty of stolen photos. A new photo proves nothing.

options.label: Ask for a photo of his passport
options.feedback: A document photo is easy to fake. It proves nothing.

options.label: Trust him, because he writes every day
options.feedback: Writing every day is the scammer's job. Sometimes he writes to several people at once.

scenes.explain: A video call and a reverse image search are the two simplest checks. If he avoids both, stop.

scenes.prompt: Your online contact asks for money. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Do not send money or crypto
Talk to your family or a friend
Report and block the profile on the platform

scenes.explain: First stop the money, then check and talk. If money has already gone, contact your bank and the police at once.

points: Never send money or crypto to someone you have not met in person.
Avoiding video calls, investment offers and requests for secrecy are warnings.
Reverse image search the photo and talk to your family.
